category_title: Older preschool children expressing specific anxieties about environmental and relational consistency
student_description: This student experiences high anxiety regarding environmental transitions, specifically fearing the loss of familiar materials, spaces, and relationships. Their distress manifests as repetitive, concrete questioning about what will happen to specific items and people. They uniquely require direct reassurance and tangible, participatory activities—such as labeling items, journaling, and dramatic play—to gain a sense of control and consistency during the transition.

criteria.rationale: Engaging in dramatic play over time allows this student to physically process and problem-solve the mechanics of the move, reducing their environmental anxiety.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan incorporates sustained dramatic play activities using physical props (e.g., boxes, makeshift trucks, spatial outlines) where the student can actively role-play the moving process.
